items.title: Twelve test helpers still read a served page with a fixed 5 s timeout and swallow the timeout into an empty response (a loaded Windows runner failed one of the family)
items.discussion: CI run 43546495690 (next 8af7c7a2, 2026-11-13), windows 3/4: `document::a_head_hatch_on_a_supplied_shell_now_rides_the_served_page` asserted on an EMPTY page; `document.rs`'s `http_get` fixed at next 5267caff (the bound is `support::run_liveness()`, a read that does not complete panics with what had arrived)
items.body: The same shape remains at twelve sites: `set_read_timeout(Some(Duration::from_secs(5)))` (one at 10 s) followed by a read whose error is ignored: `asset_bundle.rs:159`, `hmr.rs:278` and `:312`, `init.rs:630`, `serve_build.rs:199` and `:239`, `ssr_fullstack.rs:100`, `service_layer.rs:1700`, `:1733` and `:3611`, `split.rs:928`. On a loaded runner each can fail an assertion about content on an empty string, which reads as a product bug. Move ONE helper into `tests/support/` (a GET bounded by `run_liveness()` that fails by name on a timeout or a reset) and use it everywhere; check each site's intent first (a few may read a stream that is MEANT to stay open, where the timeout ends the read by design: those need a different helper, not a longer clock).
